coelophysis:enwiki:7.title: Coelophysis (Formerly assigned material and taxa, part 2)

facts.statement: Coelophysis is considered one of the earliest known dinosaur genera.
facts.quote: It is one of the earliest known dinosaur genera.

facts.statement: The type species Coelophysis bauri was described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1889, originally having been placed in the genus Coelurus in 1887.
facts.quote: The type species C. bauri, originally placed in the genus Coelurus by Edward Drinker Cope in 1887, was described by the latter in 1889.

facts.statement: The names Longosaurus and Rioarribasaurus are considered synonymous with the genus Coelophysis.
facts.quote: The names Longosaurus and Rioarribasaurus are synonymous with Coelophysis.

facts.statement: Cope named two new species from his New Mexican collection: Coelurus longicollis based on multiple vertebrae and a femur, and Coelurus bauri, named after Georg Baur, based on the same skeletal regions.
facts.quote: Cope chose to name two new species from his collection of New Mexican material, the first being Coelurus longicollis for multiple vertebrae and a femur, while the second was Coelurus bauri, named after German paleontologist Georg Baur, included the same regions of the skeleton.

facts.statement: In July 1887, Cope reclassified his New Mexican material from Coelurus to the genus Tanystrophaeus based on vertebral similarities, creating the combinations Tanystrophaeus longicollis and Tanystrophaeus bauri.
facts.quote: Following this description, Cope reclassified his New Mexican material in July 1887 from Coelurus to the German taxon Tanystrophaeus based on the similarities of the vertebrae, creating the new combinations Tanystrophaeus longicollis and Tanysteophaeus bauri.

facts.statement: Cope realized that the vertebrae he attributed to Tanystrophaeus were not definitively caudal vertebrae, leading him to create a new genus name for the species.
facts.quote: Following this, Cope came to the realization that the vertebrae of Tanystrophaeus he considered similar to the New Mexican species were not definitively caudal vertebrae, and as a result the species were in need of a new genus name.

facts.statement: In 1889, Cope described the new genus Coelophysis containing three species, with the name derived from the Ancient Greek words for 'hollow' and 'form'.
facts.quote: As a result, in 1889 Cope described the new genus Coelophysis, with three species C. longicollis, C. bauri, and C. willistoni, the name being a combination of the Ancient Greek words κοῖλος (koilos), "hollow", and φύσεις (fysis), "form".

facts.statement: In 1986, Kevin Padian revisited the type material of Coelophysis to identify which specimens were referred to which species by Cope and Huene, and identified previously undescribed material in the Cope collection.
facts.quote: In 1986 American paleontologist Kevin Padian revisited the type material of Coelophysis and identified which material was referred to which species by Cope and Huene in their studies, and identified some material in the Cope collection that had yet to be described.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Megapnosaurus was once a species within Coelophysis, but it is now considered a valid genus.
facts.quote: Megapnosaurus was once considered to be a species within this genus, but this interpretation has been challenged and the genus Megapnosaurus is now considered valid.

facts.statement: The Ghost Ranch excavation yielded hundreds of Coelophysis skeletons in a single concentration, described as the greatest Triassic find in North America.
facts.quote: upon the return of Simpson and Fish to the locality the former stated that "this was the greatest find ever made in the Triassic of North America".

facts.statement: Excavations at the Ghost Ranch Coelophysis quarry continued through 1947 and 1948 by the American Museum of Natural History crew.
facts.quote: Excavations of the Ghost Ranch Coelophysis quarry were continued throughout 1947 and 1948 by the crew of the AMNH

facts.statement: The quarry was reopened and worked between 1981 and 1982, excavating 16 large blocks weighing 6 to 10 short tons each.
facts.quote: The quarry was worked from 1981 to 1982, with 16 large blocks of 6 to 10 short ton excavated, and all but one block being removed.

facts.statement: All material from the Ghost Ranch quarry was classified as a single species of Coelophysis known from hundreds of individuals.
facts.quote: All of the Ghost Ranch material was thus described as part of a single species known from hundreds of individuals of various ages and sizes

facts.statement: Some researchers debate the validity of Coelophysis as a distinct genus, suggesting it is a 'metataxon' lacking unique characteristics.
facts.quote: Padian instead considered it a "metataxon" or otherwise lacking unique characteristics of its own and having anatomy primitive to Theropoda.

facts.statement: Variation in proportions among individuals of the same size suggests the existence of 'robust' and 'gracile' morphs within Coelophysis.
facts.quote: with some additional variation in proportions of individuals at the same size that gave the suggestion of a "robust" and "gracile" morph.

facts.statement: Coelophysis fossils from Ghost Ranch were found in the Chinle Formation, which was believed to be of Norian age at the time of discovery.
facts.quote: All of the excavations at Ghost Ranch took place within the upper sandstone level of the Chinle Formation, believed to be Norian in age at the time

facts.statement: Paleontologists Adrian P. Hunt and Spencer G. Lucas proposed that the complete specimens from the Ghost Ranch Whitaker Quarry represented a new taxon named Rioarribasaurus colberti.
facts.quote: As a result, they determined that a new taxon was required for the very complete specimens from Ghost Ranch (what they referred to as the Whitaker Quarry), for which they named Rioarribasaurus colberti.

facts.statement: The name Rioarribasaurus refers to Rio Arriba County, and the species name colberti honors the paleontologist Colbert.
facts.quote: The genus name referred to the Rio Arriba County where the fossils were discovered, while the species name was in honor of Colbert for his work excavating and describing the material.

facts.statement: The complete skeleton AMNH 7224 was designated the holotype for Rioarribasaurus, a taxon that included all Ghost Ranch specimens collected between 1947 and 1982.
facts.quote: The complete skeleton AMNH 7224, mounted on display at the museum, was selected as the holotype of Rioarribasaurus, and all the Ghost Ranch specimens collected from 1947 to 1982 were referred to the taxon as they lacked differences beyond sexual or growth-related variation.

facts.statement: A 1996 study by Hunt, Lucas, Sullivan, and Heckert concluded that the original Coelophysis collection site was a different geological level than the Ghost Ranch quarry.
facts.quote: In a following study in 1996, Hunt and Lucas as well as American paleontologists Robert M. Sullivan and Andrew Heckert established that the locality where Baldwin collected Coelophysis was not the same deposit or level as the dinosaur quarry as Colbert had believed.

facts.statement: Hunt and Lucas argued that Coelophysis lived in the Revueltian-age Petrified Forest Formation, while Rioarribasaurus lived in the older Apachean-age Rock Point Formation.
facts.quote: According to the stratigraphy of Sullivan, Lucas and colleagues, Coelophysis would therefore be from the Revueltian-age Petrified Forest Formation, with Rioarribasaurus from the Apachean-age Rock Point Formation.

facts.statement: Radiometric dating places the Coelophysis collection sites at the Baldwin localities at 211.9±0.7 million years ago during the late Norian.
facts.quote: The Baldwin sites as part of the Petrified Forest Member radiometrically dated to 211.9±0.7 million years ago in the late Norian.

facts.statement: Hunt and Lucas believed that none of the material from the three species possessed unique characteristics supporting their synonymy with Coelophysis bauri or other theropods.
facts.quote: None of the material of the three species was believed by Hunt and Lucas to bear any unique characteristics that could support their synonymy to C. bauri or any other theropod.

facts.statement: Colbert and colleagues petitioned the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature to designate AMNH 7224 as a neotype for Coelophysis bauri to resolve confusion and preserve the name for the Ghost Ranch material.
facts.quote: As such, Colbert and other paleontologists petitioned to the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature to replace the lectotype of Coelophysis bauri with AMNH 7224 as a neotype, thereby making Coelophysis bauri and Rioarribasaurus colberti objective synonyms, giving Coelophysis a much better type specimen, and preserving the use of Coelophysis for the Ghost Ranch material as it had been since its discovery in 1947.

facts.statement: In 1993, Gregory S. Paul suggested that Coelophysis was indeterminate and proposed combining Rioarribasaurus and Syntarsus into the name Syntarsus colberti.
facts.quote: American paleoartist Gregory S. Paul also published in 1993 the opinion that Coelophysis was indeterminate, but that Rioarribasaurus and Syntarsus belonged to the same genus, creating the combination Syntarsus colberti.

facts.statement: The International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature voted in 1996 to designate AMNH 7224 as the neotype of Coelophysis and rejected the name Rioarribasaurus.
facts.quote: In the end, the ICZN voted in 1996 to designate the complete specimen AMNH 7224 as the neotype of Coelophysis and disposed of the name Rioarribasaurus, declaring the latter a nomen rejectum, or "rejected name".

facts.statement: Coelophysis was designated a nomen conservandum, resolving the taxonomic confusion regarding its status.
facts.quote: The name Coelophysis became a nomen conservandum ("conserved name"), and thus the confusion and uncertainty surrounding the status of Coelophysis was resolved.

facts.statement: In 1922, Case described the first material of Coelophysis found outside New Mexico, consisting of vertebrae collected in 1921 from the Dockum Formation in Crosby County, Texas.
facts.quote: In 1922 Case described the first supposed material of Coelophysis from outside New Mexico with the referral of a series of vertebrae he collected in 1921 from Dockum Formation of Crosby County, Texas.

facts.statement: In 1958, Colbert and Donald Baird rediscovered a specimen containing bone impressions of an early dinosaur, leading to comparisons suggesting it might be synonymous with Coelophysis.
facts.quote: Following the rediscovery of a specimen containing the bone impressions of an early dinosaur by Colbert and Donald Baird in 1958, Coelophysis was first compared to Podokesaurus as potentially synonymous.

facts.statement: In 1983, a partial skeleton of a theropod was found at Cross Quarry in the Orphan Mesa region, a site named after its discoverer Robert Cross where the original Coelophysis material may have been collected by Baldwin.
facts.quote: In 1983 another partial skeleton of a theropod was found from the Orphan Mesa region where it is possible Baldwin collected the original Coelophysis material, at a site named Cross Quarry after its discoverer Robert Cross.

facts.statement: Independent work by Sterling Nesbitt, Randall Irmis, and William Parker in 2007 upheld the identification of Eucoelophysis as a silesaurid, distant from Coelophysis and the Baldwin material.
facts.quote: The identification of Eucoelophysis as a silesaurid, distant from Coelophysis and the Baldwin material, was upheld by independent work by American paleontologists Sterling Nesbitt, Randall Irmis and William Parker in 2007.

facts.statement: In 2024, a petition was submitted to the ICZN requesting that the name Syntarsus be retained for the theropod.
facts.quote: In 2024, it has been petitioned to the ICZN that Syntarsus be retained for the name of the theropod.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses of Coelophysidae found that S. rhodesiensis is not the sister taxon to Coelophysis, leading to the use of the name Megapnosaurus in those cases.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analyses of Coelophysidae have found that S. rhodesiensis is not the sister taxon to Coelophysis, so the name Megapnosaurus has been used in those cases.

facts.statement: Coelophysis was a lightly built dinosaur that measured up to 3 meters in length and stood more than one meter tall at the hips.
facts.quote: This lightly built dinosaur measured up to 3 m long and was more than a meter tall at the hips.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the weight of Coelophysis at 15 kg for the gracile form, 20 kg for the robust form, and later revised the estimate to 25 kg.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul (1988) estimated the weight of the gracile form at 15 kg and the weight of the robust form at 20 kg, but later presented a higher estimate of 25 kg.

facts.statement: Coelophysis was a bipedal, carnivorous theropod dinosaur known as a fast and agile runner.
facts.quote: Coelophysis was a bipedal, carnivorous, theropod dinosaur and a fast, agile runner.

facts.statement: Coelophysis bauri possessed a furcula, representing the earliest known example of this bone in dinosaurs.
facts.quote: C. bauri had a furcula (wishbone), the earliest known example in a dinosaur.

facts.statement: Coelophysis had four digits on its hand, but only three were functional as the fourth was embedded in the flesh.
facts.quote: It had only three functional digits, with the fourth being embedded in the flesh of the hand.

facts.statement: The feet of Coelophysis ended in three toes and featured a raised dewclaw.
facts.quote: The leg ended in a three-toed foot (pes) with a raised dewclaw (hallux).

facts.statement: Coelophysis had a semi-rigid lattice structure in its tail vertebrae designed to prevent the tail from moving up and down.
facts.quote: The tail had an unusual structure within its interlocking prezygapophysis of its vertebrae, which formed a semi-rigid lattice, apparently to stop the tail from moving up and down.

facts.statement: Coelophysis had a long, narrow head approximately 270 mm long with large forward-facing eyes providing excellent depth perception.
facts.quote: Coelophysis had a long and narrow head (approximately 270 mm), with large, forward-facing eyes that afforded it stereoscopic vision and, as a result, excellent depth perception.

facts.statement: A 2004 study of a juvenile Coelophysis bauri concluded it was a diurnal, visually oriented predator with vision superior to most lizards.
facts.quote: Rinehart et al. (2004) described the complete scleral ring found for a juvenile Coelophysis bauri (specimen NMMNH P-4200) and compared it to data on the scleral rings of reptiles (including birds), concluding that Coelophysis was a diurnal, visually oriented predator.

facts.statement: The eyes of Coelophysis were similar to those of eagles and hawks, possessing a high power of accommodation.
facts.quote: The eyes of Coelophysis appear to be the closest to those of eagles and hawks, with a high power of accommodation.

facts.statement: Coelophysis had an elongated snout with large openings that reduced skull weight while narrow bone struts maintained structural integrity.
facts.quote: Coelophysis had an elongated snout with large fenestrae that helped to reduce skull weight, while narrow struts of bones preserved the structural integrity of the skull.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Coelophysis bauri is the same species as Megapnosaurus rhodesiensis, with many paleontologists refuting this identification.
facts.quote: Several paleontologists consider Coelophysis bauri to be the same dinosaur as Megapnosaurus rhodesiensis (formerly Syntarsus). However, this has been refuted by many paleontologists.

facts.statement: Downs concluded in 2000 that C. bauri differs from C. rhodesiensis in cervical length, leg proportions, and caudal vertebral anatomy.
facts.quote: Downs (2000) concluded that C. bauri differs from C. rhodesiensis in cervical length, proximal and distal leg proportions, and proximal caudal vertebral anatomy.

facts.statement: Bristowe and Raath concluded in 2004 that C. bauri differs from M. rhodesiensis by having a longer maxillary tooth row.
facts.quote: Bristowe and Raath (2004) concluded that C. bauri differs from M. rhodesiensis in having a longer maxillary tooth row.

facts.statement: Barta et al. concluded in 2018 that C. bauri differs from M. rhodesiensis by possessing a fifth metacarpal.
facts.quote: Barta et al. (2018) concluded that C. bauri differed from M. rhodesiensis in that it bears its 5th metacarpal.

facts.statement: Griffin concluded in 2018 that C. bauri differs from M. rhodesiensis in several aspects of limb musculature.
facts.quote: Griffin (2018) concluded that C. bauri differs from M. rhodesiensis in several differences in the musculature of the limbs.

facts.statement: Coelophysis bauri is classified within the theropod family Coelophysidae alongside the genus Sarcosaurus.
facts.quote: Coelophysis bauri was placed along with Sarcosaurus as coelophysids

facts.statement: Coelophysis is a genus containing only one valid species, C. bauri.
facts.quote: Coelophysis is a distinct taxonomic unit (genus), composed of the single species C. bauri

facts.statement: The species C. longicollis and C. willistoni are no longer considered valid because they are undiagnostic.
facts.quote: Two additional originally described species, C. longicollis and C. willistoni, are now considered dubious and undiagnostic

facts.statement: The species M. rhodesiensis, once referred to Coelophysis, is now likely classified as a distinct genus.
facts.quote: M. rhodesiensis was referred to Coelophysis for several years, but it is likely its own genus

facts.statement: Coelophysis kayentakatae is a possible species that was previously assigned to the genus Megapnosaurus.
facts.quote: A third possible species is Coelophysis kayentakatae, previously referred to the genus Megapnosaurus

facts.statement: Recent analyses suggest that "Syntarsus" kayentakatae belongs to its own genus because it is distantly related to Coelophysis and Megapnosaurus.
facts.quote: In recent phylogenetic analyses, "Syntarsus" kayentakatae has been shown to be distantly related to Coelophysis and Megapnosaurus, suggesting that it belongs to its own genus

facts.statement: Coelophysis possessed blade-like, recurved, sharp, and finely serrated teeth on both edges, typical of predatory dinosaurs.
facts.quote: The teeth of Coelophysis were typical of predatory dinosaurs, as they were blade-like, recurved, sharp, jagged, and finely serrated on both the anterior and posterior edges

facts.statement: Coelophysis bauri had approximately 26 teeth in its upper jaw and 27 teeth in its lower jaw.
facts.quote: Coelophysis bauri has approximately 26 teeth on the maxillary bone of the upper jaw and 27 teeth on the dentary bone of the lower jaw

facts.statement: The weak arms and small teeth of Coelophysis suggest it preyed on animals substantially smaller than itself.
facts.quote: The "weak" arms and small teeth in this genus suggested that Coelophysis preyed upon animals that were substantially smaller than itself

facts.statement: Coelophysis may have hunted in packs to tackle prey larger than itself.
facts.quote: It may also have hunted in packs to tackle larger prey

facts.statement: Evidence of cannibalism was found in specimen NMMNH P-44551, which contained regurgitated material including fragments of juvenile Coelophysis teeth and jaw bones.
facts.quote: In 2009, new evidence of cannibalism came to light when additional preparation of previously excavated matrix revealed regurgitate material in and around the mouth of Coelophysis specimen NMMNH P-44551

facts.statement: Analysis of specimen AMNH 7224 showed that the volume of juvenile bones found inside it was 17 times greater than the animal's maximum estimated stomach volume, suggesting they were not eaten.
facts.quote: Gay examined the bones of juveniles found within the thoracic cavity of AMNH 7224 and calculated that the total volume of these bones was 17 times greater than the maximum estimated stomach volume of the Coelophysis specimen

facts.statement: Over 1,000 specimens of Coelophysis were discovered at the Whitaker quarry at Ghost Ranch.
facts.quote: The discovery of over 1,000 specimens of Coelophysis at the Whitaker quarry at Ghost Ranch has suggested gregarious behavior to researchers

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the large congregation of Coelophysis at Ghost Ranch may have gathered to feed or drink before being buried by a flash flood or drought.
facts.quote: Some of the evidence from the taphonomy of the site indicates that these animals may have been gathered together to feed or drink from a depleted water hole or to feed on a spawning run of fish, being later buried in a catastrophic flash flood or a drought

facts.statement: The discovery of 30 specimens of C. rhodesiensis found together in Zimbabwe has led some paleontologists to suggest Coelophysis was gregarious.
facts.quote: With 30 specimens of C. rhodesiensis found together in Zimbabwe, some palaeontologists have suggested that Coelophysis was indeed gregarious

facts.statement: Coelophysis likely reached sexual maturity between its second and third year of life and attained a full length of just over 10 feet by its eighth year.
facts.quote: Coelophysis likely reached sexual maturity between the second and third year of life and reached its full size, just above 10 feet in length, by its eighth year.

facts.statement: Historically, it was thought that Coelophysis hatchlings had to fend for themselves immediately after hatching.
facts.quote: It was also thought that, as soon as they were hatched, they would have to fend for themselves.

facts.statement: Recent research suggests that distinct morphs in Coelophysis may simply represent individual variation in growth rates rather than sexual dimorphism.
facts.quote: However, more recent research based on analysis of growth series has found that C. bauri and C. rhodesiensis had highly variable growth between individuals, with some specimens being larger in their immature phase than smaller adults were when completely mature.

facts.statement: The average Coelophysis egg was estimated to be 31–33.5 mm across its minor diameter, with females laying 24 to 26 eggs per clutch.
facts.quote: It was estimated that average egg of Coelophysis was 31–33.5 millimeters across its minor diameter and that each female would lay between 24 and 26 eggs in each clutch.

facts.statement: Edwin H. Colbert suggested that theropod footprints of the ichnogenus Grallator found in the Connecticut River Valley may have been made by Coelophysis.
facts.quote: Edwin H. Colbert has suggested that the theropod footprints referred to the ichnogenus Grallator, located in the Connecticut River Valley across Connecticut and Massachusetts, may have been made by Coelophysis.

facts.statement: C. rhodesiensis fossils have been recovered from the Upper Elliot Formation in South Africa and the Forest Sandstone Formation in Zimbabwe.
facts.quote: C. rhodesiensis has been recovered in the Upper Elliot Formation in the Cape and Free State provinces of South Africa, as well as the Chitake River bonebed quarry at the Forest Sandstone Formation in Zimbabwe.

facts.statement: Research indicates that Coelophysis lived in floodplain environments with distinct dry and wet seasons.
facts.quote: Therrien and Fastovsky (2001) examined the paleoenvironment of Coelophysis and other early theropods from Petrified Forest National Park in Arizona and determined that this genus lived in an environment that consisted of floodplains marked by distinct dry and wet seasons.

facts.statement: The large number of Coelophysis specimens found together at Ghost Ranch was likely caused by a flash flood that swept them away and buried them simultaneously.
facts.quote: The multitude of specimens deposited so closely together at Ghost Ranch was probably the result of a flash flood that swept away a large number of Coelophysis and buried them quickly and simultaneously.

facts.statement: Coelophysis was the second dinosaur to travel to space, with a skull from the Carnegie Museum of Natural History aboard the Space Shuttle Endeavour mission STS-89 on January 22, 1998.
facts.quote: Coelophysis was the second dinosaur in space, following Maiasaura (STS-51-F). A Coelophysis skull from the Carnegie Museum of Natural History was aboard the Space Shuttle Endeavour mission STS-89 when it left the atmosphere on 22 January 1998.

facts.statement: Coelophysis was designated the official state fossil of New Mexico in 1981 and serves as the logo of the New Mexico Museum of Natural History.
facts.quote: Since the discovery of Coelophysis fossils more than 100 years ago, it is one of the best-known dinosaurs in literature. It was designated as the official state fossil of New Mexico in 1981 and is now the logo of the New Mexico Museum of Natural History.

facts.statement: The genus Coelophysis was described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1887.
facts.quote: genus_authority = Cope, 1887

facts.statement: Coelophysis lived during the late Triassic and early Jurassic periods, approximately 203 to 196 million years ago.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Triásico y a principios del Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 203 a 196 millones de años

facts.statement: Fossils of Coelophysis have been found in North America and Africa.
facts.quote: en Norteamérica y África

facts.statement: The generic name Coelophysis refers to the hollow bones found in its legs.
facts.quote: Su nombre genérico se debe a que los huesos de sus patas eran huecos

facts.statement: Coelophysis measured between 2.5 and 3 meters in length and reached about one meter in height at the hips.
facts.quote: llegaba a medir de 2,5 a 3 metros de longitud, alcanzaba el metro de altura a la cadera

facts.statement: In 1988, Paul estimated the weight of the gracile form at 15 kilograms and the robust form at 20 kilograms.
facts.quote: Paul en 1988 estimó el peso de la forma grácil a 15 kilogramos, y el de la forma robusta a 20 kilogramos

facts.statement: C. bauri possessed a furcula, representing the first known example of this structure in a dinosaur.
facts.quote: C. bauri tenía una furcula, el primer ejemplo conocido en un dinosaurio

facts.statement: Coelophysis retained the ancestral condition of having four digits in its hand.
facts.quote: Coelophysis también conserva la condición ancestral de poseer cuatro dígitos en la mano

facts.statement: The hind limb ended in a three-toed foot with an elevated hallux.
facts.quote: La extremidad posterior terminó en un pie de tres dedos, con un hallux elevado

facts.statement: The tail had an unusual structure in the prezygapophyseal joints of its vertebrae, forming a semi-rigid lattice.
facts.quote: La cola tenía una estructura inusual en las uniones prezigapofisis de sus vértebras, que formaban un enrejado semirrígido

facts.statement: The tail's lattice structure may have helped the animal maneuver at high speeds.
facts.quote: puede haber ayudado cuando el animal maniobraba a gran velocidad

facts.statement: Coelophysis had a long, narrow head measuring approximately 270 millimeters.
facts.quote: tenía una cabeza larga y estrecha de aproximadamente 270 milímetros

facts.statement: Research concluded that Coelophysis was a diurnal predator oriented towards vision.
facts.quote: concluyeron que Coelophysis era un depredador diurno orientado a la vista

facts.statement: Coelophysis's vision was superior to that of most lizards and comparable to modern birds of prey.
facts.quote: La visión de Coelophysis era superior a la visión de la mayoría de las lagartijas, y comparable con la de las aves rapaces modernas

facts.statement: Coelophysis's eyes appear most similar to those of eagles and hawks, possessing high accommodation power.
facts.quote: Los ojos de Coelophysis parecen ser los más cercanos a los de águilas y halcones, con un alto poder de acomodación

facts.statement: Data suggested that Coelophysis had poor night vision.
facts.quote: Los datos también sugirieron una visión nocturna deficiente

facts.statement: Coelophysis had an elongated snout with large openings that helped reduce skull weight.
facts.quote: El Coelophysis tenía un hocico alargado con grandes ventanas que ayudaban a reducir el peso del cráneo

facts.statement: Its mouth was filled with numerous curved teeth featuring serrated edges on both the front and back.
facts.quote: Su boca se coronaba de una gran cantidad de dientes curvados, con bordes aserrados en los bordes anterior y posterior

facts.statement: Its neck had a pronounced S-shaped curve similar to modern birds, acting like a spring to increase bite speed.
facts.quote: El cuello tenía una curva sigmoidea pronunciada, similar al de varias aves modernas, que actuaba como un muelle

facts.statement: Evidence suggests it ate meat, likely small animals such as lizards found near its fossils.
facts.quote: demuestra que se alimentaba de carne, probablemente animales pequeño, como los lagartos que fueron encontrados junto a ellos

facts.statement: Researchers suggest this small dinosaur may have lived in large herds to hunt larger prey.
facts.quote: Además se piensa que es posible que este pequeño dinosaurio viviera en grandes manadas, lo que le permitiría cazar animales mayores

facts.statement: Diagnostic features include the absence of a compensated rostral process of the upper jaw and a strongly posterior quadrate bone.
facts.quote: la ausencia de un proceso rostral compensado del maxilar superior, el cuadrado es fuertemente caudal

facts.statement: It possesses a small external mandibular fenestra measuring 9-10% of the jaw length.
facts.quote: una pequeña fenestra mandibular externa, que es 9-10% de la longitud mandibular

facts.statement: The anteroposterior length of the ventral lacrimal process is greater than 30% of its height.
facts.quote: la longitud anteroposterior del proceso lagrimal ventral es mayor que 30% de su altura

facts.statement: While some paleontologists consider Coelophysis bauri and Coelophysis rhodesiensis to be the same animal, Downs refuted this in 2000.
facts.quote: Varios paleontólogos consideran que Coelophysis bauri es el mismo dinosaurio que Coelophysis rhodesiensis, anteriormente "Syntarsus", alternativamente "Megapnosaurus", sin embargo, esto ha sido refutado por Downs en 2000

facts.statement: Tykoski and Rowe concluded in 2004 that C. bauri differs from C. rhodesiensis by lacking a hole at the base of the nasal process of the premaxilla.
facts.quote: Tykoski y Rowe en 2004 concluyeron que C. bauri difiere de C. rhodesiensis en que carece de un hoyo en la base del proceso nasal del premaxilar

facts.statement: C. kayentakatae is recognized by a crest on the nasolacrimal bones and the fusion of the fibula to the calcaneus in adults.
facts.quote: A C. kayetakatae, se lo reconoce por una cresta en los nasolacrimales y la fusión del peroné al calcáneo en los adultos

facts.statement: The presence of a similar crest and shared habitat has led some to hypothesize that C. kayentakatae might be a juvenile Dilophosaurus.
facts.quote: ha llevado a pensar que C. kayentakatae pudo ser un Dilophosaurus joven

facts.statement: Character descriptions from disarticulated material are significant because the anteorbital window length depends on correctly interpreting the lacrimal position.
facts.quote: Es significativo que estos caracteres fueron descritos del material desarticulado, porque la longitud de la ventana anteorbital depende de que la posición del lacrimal sea interpretada correctamente

facts.statement: It is one of the oldest dinosaurs for which the presence of feathers has been suggested.
facts.quote: Además de ser uno de los dinosaurios más antiguos que se ha sugerido la presencia de plumas

facts.statement: Coelophysis was discovered in 1881 by amateur fossil collector David Baldwin working for E. D. Cope.
facts.quote: Coelophysis fue descubierto en 1881 por David Baldwin un coleccionista aficionado de fósiles que trabajaba para E. D. Cope

facts.statement: It was found in Triassic strata of the Chinle Formation in northwestern New Mexico, southwestern United States.
facts.quote: en estratos del Triásico de la formación Chinle en el noroeste de Nuevo México, suroeste de Estados Unidos

facts.statement: The name Coelophysis comes from Greek words meaning 'hollow' and 'form', referring to its hollow vertebrae.
facts.quote: El nombre Coelophysis proviene del griego κοιλος / koilos, que significa 'hueco', y φυσις / physis, que significa 'forma', por lo tanto, "forma hueca" que es una referencia a sus vértebras huecas

facts.statement: In 1947, George Whitaker found a substantial bone bed of Coelophysis fossils at Ghost Ranch, New Mexico.
facts.quote: En 1947, George Whitaker, el asistente de Edwin H. Colbert, en Ghost Ranch Nuevo México, encontró un "lecho de huesos" sustancial de fósiles de Coelophysis

facts.statement: The numerous and well-preserved Ghost Ranch specimens led to one becoming the type specimen for the entire genus.
facts.quote: Los especímenes de Ghost Ranch fueron tan numerosos, incluidos muchos especímenes bien conservados y completamente articulados, que uno de ellos se ha convertido en el diagnóstico, o espécimen tipo para todo el género

facts.statement: Its presence in Africa and the southwestern US suggests it migrated across continents that were connected in Pangea.
facts.quote: Este pequeño depredador tenía las mismas características básicas encontradas en dinosaurios tempranos, y su aparición en [África y al sudoeste los EE.UU. indica que emigró a través de los continentes

facts.statement: Footprints most attributed to C. rhodesiensis were discovered in Rhodesia in 1915.
facts.quote: Las huellas de dinosaurios que más se atribuyeron a C. rhodesiensis fueron descubiertas en Rhodesia en 1915

facts.statement: These footprints were found in the Nyamandhlovu Sandstone Formation, deposited in the Late Triassic approximately 235 to 201 million years ago.
facts.quote: Estas huellas fueron descubiertas en la Formación de Areniscas de Nyamandhlovu, en arenisca roja eólica que se depositó en el Triásico Superior hace aproximadamente 235 a 201 millones de años

facts.statement: Coelophysis was the second dinosaur to go to space, following Maiasaura.
facts.quote: Coelophysis fue el segundo dinosaurio en el espacio, siguiendo a Maiasaura

facts.statement: A Coelophysis skull from the Carnegie Museum of Natural History flew aboard the Space Shuttle STS-89, exiting the atmosphere on January 22, 1998.
facts.quote: Un cráneo de Coelophysis del Museo Carnegie de Historia Natural estaba a bordo de la misión STS-89 del transbordador espacial STS-89 cuando salió de la atmósfera el 22 de enero de 1998

facts.statement: It was designated the official state fossil of New Mexico.
facts.quote: Fue designado como el fósil estatal oficial de Nuevo México

facts.statement: C. bauri specifically became the state fossil of New Mexico in 1981.
facts.quote: Coelophysis bauri también se convirtió en un fósil estatal de Nuevo México en 1981

facts.statement: Coelophysis appeared in the first episode of the BBC series Walking with Dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Coelophysis también apareció en el primer episodio de la serie de la BBC Walking with Dinosaurs

facts.statement: Its parent group is Coelophysinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Coelophysinae

facts.statement: It belongs to the family Coelophysidae.
facts.quote: Family: Coelophysidae

facts.statement: It is classified under the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: It lived from the Norian to the Sinemurian stages, between 227.3 and 192.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Sinemurian (227.3 to 192.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Research in 2026 reconstructed the optimal jumping performance of C. bauri as similar to that of the elegant crested tinamou.
facts.quote: Charles, Polet & Hutchinson (2026) reconstruct the optimal jumping performance of Coelophysis bauri as overall similar to that of extant elegant crested tinamou

facts.statement: Researchers reported evidence suggesting the long, mobile tail impacted jumping performance.
